title: Courtyard Domino Tilings
description:
## Task

A courtyard is a `rows` by `cols` grid of square cells. Some cells are holes (fountains) and must stay uncovered; every other cell must be covered by a domino that spans exactly two edge-adjacent cells, with no overlaps and nothing outside the grid. Count the ways to do so, modulo 1,000,000,007.

## Input

- `rows`, `cols` — the grid size.
- `holes` — a list of distinct `[row, col]` pairs (0-based) that stay uncovered.

## Output

The number of valid tilings modulo 1000000007. Zero if there is none; a grid with every cell a hole has exactly one (empty) tiling.

## Example

```python
courtyard_tilings(2, 3, [])  # returns 3
courtyard_tilings(3, 3, [[1, 1]])  # returns 2
courtyard_tilings(3, 3, [])  # returns 0
```

## Constraints

- 1 ≤ `rows` ≤ 12, 1 ≤ `cols` ≤ 12
- Enumerating placements one by one is far too slow on the larger grids; process the grid cell by cell while remembering only the frontier.
signature: def courtyard_tilings(rows: int, cols: int, holes: list[list[int]]) -> int
